links.comparator_used: Encounters without AI scribe availability or use (clinician-authored patient instructions documentation)
links.effect: 10.5 percentage-point increase with AI scribe availability (P = .018); encounter-level AI use aOR 4.32 (95% CI, 4.14-4.50)
links.tradeoff: AI drafts differed substantially from final documentation (median character-level edit distance 39.7%), implying considerable clinician editing effort.
links.quote: AI scribe availability was associated with a 10.5 percentage-point increase in patient instructions documentation frequency (P = .018), and encounter-level AI use was associated with higher odds of documentation (aOR 4.32; 95% CI, 4.14-4.50).

links.comparator_used: AI-alone instructions without clinician editing (vs clinicians assisted by AI)
links.outcome: Length and text complexity of patient instructions after clinician editing
links.effect: Clinician editing increased length without meaningfully reducing complexity; median edit distance between AI drafts and final text 39.7%
links.tradeoff: Editing added length and substantial editing burden without closing the complexity gap.
links.quote: Clinician editing of AI content increased length without meaningfully reducing complexity.

design_hint: clinician review and editing of AI scribe drafts
